main_text.head: DE QUINTO CORPORE simplici, videlicet cœlo.
AN SIT?
main_text.p: Est'ne præter quatuor elementa sim-plicia quoddam corpus sim-plex quintum?
MAXIME. Prius tamen quàm istud declaremus,Libro 1. cap.2. quædam sunt annotanda.

p.i: 1. Omnia corpora naturalia sunt per se mobilia secundum locum. Probatur: Corpora naturalia sunt, quæ habent naturam. Atqui natura est principium motus in eis in quibus est. Igitur corpora naturalia habent principium motus in seipsis.

page.notes: The scan is clear. The drop capital M of "Maxime" is set as a large letter, shown here as MAXIME. The printed "Maxime" word may carry a grave accent on the e, which is hard to confirm at this resolution, so the accent is not included. The margin note is printed on two short lines, "Libro 1." and "cap.2.", with a small ornament after "cap.2."; they are given here as one note. Long s is rendered as plain s throughout. Faint show-through from the reverse side is ignored.
